summary: Schwarzman Scholars is a one-year master's programme in global affairs taught in English at Schwarzman College, Tsinghua University, in Beijing. It is aimed at young people with leadership potential from any undergraduate field, from any country. The Class of 2028-2029 starts in August 2028. The programme pays for tuition, room and board, travel to and from Beijing, health insurance and a personal stipend, together with study tours and course materials.
eligibility_notes:
Education: an undergraduate degree is required. Applicants still studying must be on track to finish all degree requirements before 1 August 2028 and the degree must be verified before orientation. Any field of study is accepted. Applicants who already hold a master's degree may apply on the same terms. Transfer students are not accepted. The undergraduate institution must be properly accredited.

Age: at least 18 and not yet 29 on 1 August 2028. The eligibility checker asks whether you were born after 1 August 1999.

Citizenship: this global route is for non-Chinese citizens with a regular passport from a country other than China. People with Chinese citizenship (mainland, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan) apply through a separate Chinese application route. The citizenship you select must match the passport you will use for the Chinese student visa. Applicants born in China or with Chinese citizen parents face extra requirements, and applicants who took another nationality after 30 April 2022 are not eligible on this route; the programme asks them to contact the admissions office. The programme cannot help you get a passport.

Academic record: there is no minimum GPA or class rank, but academic excellence is required; the strongest applicants are among the top students of their graduating class. Marital status does not count against applicants.

English: all teaching is in English. Applicants whose first language is not English must send an accepted test score: TOEFL iBT 100 out of 120 (5 on the 6-point scale), IELTS 7, Cambridge English C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 185, or Duolingo English Test 130. The test is waived after at least two years of English-language study at undergraduate level, or at master's level or higher. Some tests are valid for only two years.

Qualities assessed: leadership ability, character and integrity, academic aptitude and intellectual ability, empathy and intercultural competence, open-mindedness and entrepreneurial spirit.
age_experience_notes: At least 18 and not yet 29 on 1 August 2028. No minimum work experience is stated; applicants without full-time work are not penalised. Leadership examples should show extended efforts, not routine workplace tasks.
funding_summary: The programme states that the costs of the year in Beijing are covered by the programme: tuition and fees, room and board, travel to and from Beijing at the start and end of the academic year, in-country study tours, required course books and supplies, a Lenovo laptop, health insurance and a personal stipend. No amount is given for the stipend. There is no application fee. For interviews the programme pays economy-class airfare or train fare and, if needed, one hotel night, plus group meals. No extra funding is given for spouses or partners. The programme lasts one year.
programmes_note: One programme: a one-year master's in global affairs. Core courses fall under Global Affairs (for example Introduction to International Relations Theory and Strategy, A Critical History of Globalization, History of Global Governance), China (Institutional and Social Transformation in Contemporary China), Leadership Core, Leadership in Practice and Professional Ethics (choose one). Scholars choose electives on China and on global topics, may take courses from other English-taught master's programmes at Tsinghua (law, public health, public policy, environmental studies, business, education), and complete a capstone project. A Deep Dive in China study tour (two credits) offers business development, state-led development and rural development tracks. There are no fixed concentrations.
institutions_note: The programme is taught at Schwarzman College, Tsinghua University, in Beijing. Scholars are expected to live in the College. Some universities run their own pre-application steps with earlier deadlines; applicants should ask their university's fellowship adviser.

summary.detail: One-year master's in global affairs at Schwarzman College, Tsinghua University. Mandatory orientation in late August, graduation in early July. All courses in English. Chinese language courses are mandatory in the first module and optional after that. Any undergraduate field is accepted.

benefits.conditions: Scholars are expected to live in the College. Spouses or partners may not live or stay overnight in the College and receive no extra funding.

benefits.conditions: No application fee is charged. No extra funding for spouses or partners, who also cannot have Chinese visas sponsored by the programme or Tsinghua.

requirements.text: Online application in English, submitted electronically, including personal information, a 100-word biographical profile written in the third person, education history with cumulative GPA, language skills, up to five leadership roles, up to five awards, up to two full-time jobs, and answers on disciplinary action. Submission is final and cannot be reopened.
Resume of at most two pages.

Leadership Essay of 750 words maximum and Statement of Purpose of 500 words maximum, plus two short answers of 100 words maximum each. Word counts are strict (footnotes, headers and titles count). Uploaded as PDF or Word files. Applicants certify the essays are their own work and that no AI generator was used.

Scanned official transcripts from every degree-granting institution attended, one per degree, showing full name, institution and conferral date; current students upload their latest transcript. Transcripts not in English need full, accurate translations. Files must not be password-protected. Admitted candidates supply hard copies of final transcripts before the programme starts.

Three recommendation letters submitted online by the recommenders through a unique link: one academic, one on leadership and one of your choice. Letters must be in English or come with a translation. Emailed, mailed or applicant-uploaded letters are not accepted, and family members cannot recommend.

Video introduction of no more than one minute, shared as an unlisted link on a video platform. The admissions page lists it as a component; the instructions page calls it optional but highly recommended.
English test score: TOEFL iBT 100 (120-point scale), IELTS 7, Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 185, or Duolingo English Test 130. Report the test type, exam date and scores in the application.
requirements.conditional_rule: Applicants whose native language is not English and who have not studied in English for two or more years

requirements.text: A regular passport from a country other than China. A passport is not needed to begin but is strongly advised before submission; passport details must match the application exactly.
Interview location choice: London in late October or New York in early November.

application_steps.title: Check eligibility and contact your campus adviser
application_steps.detail: Confirm age (at least 18 and not yet 29 on 1 August 2028), degree timing and English proof. Many universities have a fellowship adviser, and some run an internal pre-application process with earlier deadlines. For the Class of 2028-2029 the global application window is April to September 2027.

application_steps.title: Prepare the application components
application_steps.detail: Write the 750-word leadership essay, 500-word statement of purpose and two 100-word answers, update a two-page resume, list leadership roles and awards, and gather official transcripts. Register three recommenders (one academic, one on leadership, one of your choice) so they receive an automatic link to submit their letters. Record a one-minute video if you wish.

application_steps.title: Submit the online application in English
application_steps.detail: Complete all sections, fix the errors flagged on the review page and submit. There is no application fee. You can submit before the letters arrive and receive an email when each letter is received. Mailed or emailed materials are not accepted and a submitted application cannot be edited.

application_steps.title: Committee review of all applications
application_steps.detail: A committee of business, government and academic leaders reviews applications. No single element counts most; all required components are weighed equally and leadership is the focus. The programme aims for variety in nationality, academic interest, gender and professional goals, and says it expects the class to be about 40 percent from the United States, 20 percent from China and 40 percent from the rest of the world. Extra unrequested materials such as portfolios are not shared with the committee.

application_steps.title: Interview in London or New York
application_steps.detail: A selected number of candidates are invited to interview in late October (London) or early November (New York) 2027. Panels usually have five or six members from business, politics, non-profits and universities; interviews last 25 minutes and include a current-events question. Attendance in person is expected and video interviews are rare. The programme pays economy-class travel and, if needed, one hotel night. Unsuccessful applicants do not receive individual feedback.

application_steps.title: Visa, final transcripts and enrolment
application_steps.detail: Tsinghua's international students office provides the visa paperwork from the spring after acceptance. You must hold a valid passport yourself. Admitted candidates supply hard copies of final transcripts, and the undergraduate degree must be verified before orientation. Orientation is in late August 2028.

application_steps.title: Live in the College and complete the year
application_steps.detail: Scholars are expected to live in the College and take part fully in the programme: core courses, electives, language courses in the first module, the Deep Dive study tour and a capstone project. The year ends with graduation in early July.
